nl.statement: A triangular array of finite-population conflict-graph experiments. For each \(n\) the population is \(\mathcal I_n=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with a known fixed simple undirected interference relation \(G_n\) on \(\mathcal I_n\), adjacency matrix \(A_{G_n}\), formal direct-effect conflict-graph operator \(\mathcal H_n=I_n+A_{G_n}\), loop-inclusive spectral radius \(\lambda_n=1+\lambda_{\max}(A_{G_n})\ge1\), and closed maximum degree \(D_n=\max_i(1+\deg_{G_n}(i))\). Potential outcomes \(Y_{n,i}(\mathbf z)\in\mathbb R\) are fixed numbers indexed by unit \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) and assignment \(\mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^{\mathcal I_n}\); there is no super-population sampling, and the endpoints are \(a_{n,i}=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf e_{n,i})\), \(b_{n,i}=Y_{n,i}(\mathbf 0_n)\), where \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) treats only \(i\) and \(\mathbf 0_n\) treats nobody. The only randomness is the family of independent desired-exposure coordinates \(U_{n,i}\in\{0,1,*\}\), taking the values \(1,0,*\) with probabilities \(p_n/2,p_n/2,t_n\), where \(p_n=(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\) and \(t_n=1-p_n\); \(\mathbb P_U\) and \(\mathbb E_U\) are the product law and expectation of these coordinates conditional on the fixed graph and potential outcomes. A unit-to-rank permutation \(\pi_n\) with inverse \(\rho_n\) fixes the reveal order and determines the strict earlier-neighbour sets \(B_{n,i}=\{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n,\ \pi_n(j)<\pi_n(i)\}\). The realized assignment \(Z_n\) is the fixed \(r=2\) conflict-graph-design output, so that on the endpoint-exposure event \(E_{n,i,k}=\{U_{n,i}=k,\ U_{n,\ell}=*\ \text{for every}\ \ell\in B_{n,i}\}\), of known probability \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\), the assignment agrees with \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) (when \(k=1\)) or with \(\mathbf 0_n\) (when \(k=0\)) on the closed \(G_n\)-neighbourhood of \(i\). The observed outcome is \(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_{n,i}(Z_n)\), the target is the finite-population direct effect \(\tau_n=n^{-1}\sum_i(a_{n,i}-b_{n,i})\), the estimator is \(T_n=n^{-1}\sum_iY_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}}\{\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,1})-\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,0})\}/q_{n,i}\) with contrast signs \(s_1=1,s_0=-1\), and its exact randomization variance and standard deviation are \(\sigma_n^2=\operatorname{Var}_U(T_n)\) and \(\sigma_n\). — HIGHEST-LEVERAGE REUSE DECISION. The world is exactly Causalean's finite-population design-based world: `FiniteDesign Omega` (a pmf on a `Fintype` assignment space) with the lightweight finite-sum layer `E X = sum_z p z * X z`, `Var`, `Cov`, `ind`, `Pr` (`DesignBased/DesignCore.lean:46`). The assignment space is `Omega n := Fin n -> Trit` with `Trit` a locally defined three-element `Fintype` for {1,0,*}; the design is `prodDesign (fun _ => tritDesign lambda)` (`DesignBased/Product.lean:49`), so independence of the desired-exposure coordinates is a STRUCTURAL fact, not an assumption -- exactly the reason to pick this world over the measure-theoretic `PO/`. `P_U`/`E_U` are `D.Pr`/`D.E`; the events `E_{n,i,k}` are `D.ind` of decidable predicates; `q_{n,i}` is proved equal to `D.Pr (E i k)` from `E_prod_block_mul` (`DesignBased/ProductBlock.lean:65`). The measure-theoretic escape hatch, if ever needed, is `DesignBased/FiniteDesignMeasure.lean` + `MeasureBridge.lean` (`D.toMeasure`, `int = E`, `.real = Pr`, `variance = Var`); the plan deliberately does NOT use it (see decisions D-ENC-3). Search trace: read `../doc/API.md` section 18 (`Experimentation/`, lines 2218-2471) end to end; grepped `Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/` for `FiniteDesign|prodDesign|compound` and confirmed `DesignCore.lean:46`, `Product.lean:49`, `TwoStage.lean:69`; `PO/` (API.md section 8h) is the measure-theoretic super-population sibling and is at the wrong abstraction for a fixed finite population with no sampling -- bypass-justified.

A fixed-constant finite-\(n\) uniformity world. Constants \(B\ge1\) (endpoint fourth-moment budget), \(c\in(0,1]\) (nondegeneracy), a universal finite \(C_0>0\), a finite \(C_{\mathrm N}(B,c)>0\) depending only on \(B\) and \(c\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) are all held fixed. An integer degree envelope \(d\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), or an integer sequence \(d_n\) with \(1\le d_n\le n\), indexes the graph-and-potential-outcome class \(\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)\). Normal approximation is measured against the standard normal distribution function \(\Phi\) in the Kolmogorov distance \(d_{\mathrm K}(X,Z)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P(X\le x)-\mathbb P(Z\le x)|\); the frontier object is the worst-case error \(K_n(d;B,c)\) over the class, and \(\mathcal R_n(d;B,c)\) denotes its exact order up to constants depending only on \(B\) and \(c\). — `Phi` is REUSED: `Causalean.Mathlib.stdNormalCDF` (`Causalean/Mathlib/Probability/StdNormalCDF.lean:47`, `= cdf (gaussianReal 0 1)`) with the full facts package already proved -- `stdNormalCDF_monotone`, `_neg` (symmetry), `_continuous`, `_strictMono`, `_pos`, `_lt_one`, `_tendsto_atBot/_atTop`, and the exact inversion pair `stdNormalCDF_probit` / `probit_stdNormalCDF` (used for `z_{1-alpha/2}` in S4). The design-layer duplicate `DesignBased.stdNormalCdf` (`GaussianCDF.lean:43`) is the same function; F2 should import the `Causalean.Mathlib` one (richer API) and, where a Causalean design-based theorem is reused verbatim, bridge with the existing agreement lemma. Since the standardized statistic is a real-valued function on a finite design, `d_K` is encoded directly as `sSup {r | exists z, r = |D.Pr (fun w => X w <= z) - stdNormalCDF z|}` -- no metric-on-measures machinery is needed. `K_n(d;B,c)` is then a second `sSup` over the class. Rayleigh` confirmed the Mathlib side has no `dK` primitive either.

The forward reveal-order martingale world attached to the design of \(\mathrm S1\). The oriented adjacency matrix \(\mathsf P_n\) has \((\mathsf P_n)_{ji}=1\) exactly when \(j\in B_{n,i}\), so rows index earlier parents and columns later children. Each desired-exposure coordinate is split into its nonnull indicator \(R_{n,i}=\mathbf 1\{U_{n,i}\ne*\}\) and, on \(\{R_{n,i}=1\}\), an independent Rademacher label \(S_{n,i}\in\{-1,1\}\) encoding the values \(1\) and \(0\). The endpoint coefficients are \(\delta_{n,i}=a_{n,i}-b_{n,i}\), \(\gamma_{n,i}=a_{n,i}+b_{n,i}\), \(w_{n,i}=|a_{n,i}|+|b_{n,i}|\), with vectors \(w_n=(w_{n,i})_i\) and \(v_n=\lambda_nw_n+\mathsf P_nw_n\). The prefix weights are \(h_{n,i}=\prod_{\ell\in B_{n,i}}(1-R_{n,\ell})/t_n\) and its truncation \(h_{n,i,<s}=\prod_{\ell\in B_{n,i}:\pi_n(\ell)<s}(1-R_{n,\ell})/t_n\), both taking values in \([0,2]\). The raw sum is \(F_n=nT_n\), the rank-indexed filtration is \(\mathcal F_{n,0}=\{\varnothing,\Omega\}\) and \(\mathcal F_{n,s}=\sigma(U_{n,\rho_n(1)},\ldots,U_{n,\rho_n(s)})\), and the rank-\(s\) predictable coefficients are \(J_{n,s}=\sum_{i:(\mathsf P_n)_{\rho_n(s),i}=1}\delta_{n,i}h_{n,i,<s}\), \(C_{n,s}=\delta_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n-J_{n,s}/t_n\), and \(G_{n,s}=\gamma_{n,\rho_n(s)}h_{n,\rho_n(s)}/p_n\). The Doob increment is \(M_{n,s}=\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s}]-\mathbb E_U[F_n\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), its predictable quadratic variation is \(Q_n=\sum_{s=1}^n\mathbb E_U[M_{n,s}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1}]\), and \(\Delta_{n,s}Q_n\) is the signed difference of \(Q_n\) between \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=1\) and \(R_{n,\rho_n(s)}=0\) with all other reveal coordinates held fixed. — The filtration \mathcal F_{n,s} is encoded WITHOUT sigma-algebras as a prefix conditional-expectation operator on the product design: `prefixCondE D S X w := (prodDesign of the coordinates outside S).E (fun u => X (glue w on S, u off S))`, i.e. partial averaging over the not-yet-revealed coordinates, with S = the first s ranks. CORRECTED REUSE ACCOUNT (round 3): the three properties this operator must supply are supported as follows. (a) PULL-OUT of an S-measurable factor is elementary linearity -- with `w` held fixed on S such a factor is a constant under the inner average, so `E_const_mul`/`E_mul_const` (`DesignBased/DesignCore.lean:103`) suffice and no product-structure lemma is needed. (b) TOWER `D.E (prefixCondE D S X) = D.E X` needs a block-splitting Fubini for `prodDesign` (`E_prod_split_block`), which is ABSENT from the Causalean design layer: the only block lemmas, `E_prod_block_mul` and `Cov_prod_disjoint_zero` (`DesignBased/ProductBlock.lean:65,122`), factor a PRODUCT of two functions living on complementary blocks and do not split a single expectation into an outer/inner pair. F2 builds it in `Helpers/PrefixFiltration.lean`, either as a `Fintype.piFinset` sum bijection or through the existing measure bridge `prodDesign_toMeasure_eq_pi` (`DesignBased/ProductMeasure.lean:74`) plus Mathlib's `Measure.pi` splitting; effort small-to-medium and promotable to Causalean. (c) INCREMENT ORTHOGONALITY is a LOCAL lemma `prefix_martingale_orthogonal`: for `s < s'`, `Cov(M_s, M_{s'}) = 0` because `M_s` is prefix-`(s'-1)`-measurable, so tower + pull-out + the conditional centering `prefixCondE (s'-1) M_{s'} = 0` give `E (M_s * M_{s'}) = 0`. It is NOT an instance of `Cov_prod_disjoint_zero`, which requires the two functions to live on DISJOINT coordinate blocks -- martingale increments share the entire earlier prefix, so that lemma does not apply. For the same reason `ProductVariance`'s `Var_prod_linear_comb` / `Cov_prod_apply_of_ne` (`DesignBased/ProductVariance.lean:90,77`) are INAPPLICABLE here: their statements are restricted to summands of the fixed single-coordinate shape `c i * g i (w i)`, whereas the reveal increments and `F_n` contain prefix products `h_{n,i}`, `h_{n,i,<s}` depending on many coordinates. That module is therefore dropped from this S-block; it survives as a legitimate reuse only in `prop:edgeless-reduction`, where `B_{n,i} = empty` forces `h_{n,i} = 1` and the summands really are single-coordinate. The correctly shaped reuse for assembling the variance identity is the SHAPE-FREE bilinear expansion `FiniteDesign.Var_linear_comb` (`DesignBased/DesignCore.lean:235`, `Var (sum_i c_i X_i) = sum_i sum_j c_i c_j Cov(X_i, X_j)`) together with `Cov_sum_left`/`Cov_sum_right`/`Cov_self`/`Cov_eq`/`E_sum` (`DesignCore.lean:174,183,156,148,114`): the diagonal terms are `E M_s^2` and the off-diagonal ones vanish by `prefix_martingale_orthogonal`. This keeps the entire Doob computation inside Finset algebra, matching the DesignBased substrate's declared philosophy, and avoids the `MeasureTheory.condExp`/`Filtration` bridge entirely. The coordinate-flip variance tensorisation `Var(Q) <= p t sum_k E (Delta_k Q)^2` used by `lem:prefix-flip-moments` is an Efron-Stein-type inequality that F2 builds in the same file (promotable to Causalean); it is likewise a consequence of the prefix-martingale decomposition of `Q_n` as a function of the reveal coordinates, not of `Var_prod_linear_comb`. The observable spectral variance-bound and feasible-inference world. The signed exposure weights are \(W_{n,i,k}=s_k\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,k})/q_{n,i}\) for \(i\in\mathcal I_n\) and \(k\in\{0,1\}\), with known covariance matrix \(\mathbf V_n=\operatorname{Cov}_U((W_{n,i,k})_{i,k})\in\mathbb S_+^{2n}\) and largest eigenvalue \(L_n=\lambda_{\max}(\mathbf V_n)\). The endpoint second-moment mass is \(H_{2,n}=\sum_i(a_{n,i}^2+b_{n,i}^2)\), estimated by \(\widehat H_{2,n}=\sum_i\sum_k(Y_{n,i}^{\mathrm{obs}})^2\mathbf 1(E_{n,i,k})/q_{n,i}\); the conservative spectral variance bound and its feasible version are \(\mathrm{VB}_n=L_nH_{2,n}/n^2\) and \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=L_n\widehat H_{2,n}/n^2\). Inference uses a fixed miscoverage level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the normal quantile \(z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\), a finite constant \(C_{\mathrm W}(B,c,\alpha)>0\) depending only on \(B\), \(c\) and \(\alpha\), and the feasible confidence set \(C_{n,\alpha}\), which is the Wald interval centred at \(T_n\) with half-width \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}\) when \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n>0\) and all of \(\mathbb R\) when \(\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n=0\). — `z_{1-alpha/2}` is REUSED as `Causalean.Mathlib.probit (1 - alpha/2)` with the exact inversion identities `stdNormalCDF_probit` / `probit_stdNormalCDF` (`Causalean/Mathlib/Probability/StdNormalCDF.lean:164,167,194`) -- this is precisely `Phi^{-1}(1-alpha/2)` and its defining property, so no local quantile is defined. `L_n` is encoded as the Rayleigh supremum `sSup {r | exists theta, ||theta||^2 = 1 and r = theta^T V_n theta}`, which for the symmetric positive-semidefinite `V_n` IS the largest eigenvalue and makes both directions used in the proof one-liners: `theta^T V theta <= L ||theta||^2` (element <= sSup after scaling) and `L <= C_0 lambda_n` (sSup of a bounded set). Mathlib's spectral-theorem route (`Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues` plus `LinearMap.IsSymmetric.hasEigenvalue_iSup_of_finiteDimensional`, `Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Rayleigh`) is available if a bridge lemma to the eigenvalue formulation is later wanted; the plan records that as optional. The ratio-consistency step of `thm:spectral-ratio` is REUSED verbatim from `Causalean.Experimentation.DesignBased.FiniteDesign.chebyshev` (`DesignBased/Chebyshev.lean:40`). Search trace: grepped `Causalean` for `eigenvalue|spectralRadius|IsHermitian` -> 22 files, all singular-value/tensor-pencil/Gram material (`Mathlib/Analysis/SingularValueWeyl.lean`, `SymmetricTensorPencil/`, `Stat/Concentration/Matrix/LocalizedGramBasic.lean`), none a top-eigenvalue-as-Rayleigh-sup helper for a PSD covariance matrix -- bypass-justified. Surveyed `Causalean/Experimentation/DesignBased/WaldPipeline.lean` (only `dependency_wald_coverage`, keyed to the Chen-Shao dependency-graph CLT premise, wrong premise for this paper) and `ExposureMappingInterference/Variance/Conservative.lean` (`htVarEst` family: the Aronow-Samii pairwise-joint estimator, not a spectral quadratic bound) -- both bypass-justified.

The critical repeated-star boundary world. A boundary constant \(\beta>0\) is fixed; the critical star size is \(k_n=\lfloor\beta n^{2/3}\rfloor\) and the number of disjoint full stars is \(m_n=\lfloor n/(k_n+1)\rfloor\), the remaining vertices being isolated padding. The limiting intensity is \(r_{\beta}=(2\beta^{3/2})^{-1}\). The boundary law is the law \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\) of \(\sqrt{8/9}\,Z_0-(N_{r_{\beta}}-r_{\beta})/(3\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\), where \(Z_0\) is standard normal and \(N_{r_{\beta}}\) is a Poisson variable of mean \(r_{\beta}\) independent of \(Z_0\). It has variance one and third cumulant \(-1/(27\sqrt{r_{\beta}})\ne0\), so it is not \(\mathcal N(0,1)\). — MAJOR REUSE FOUND BY PUSH-SEARCH. `Z_0` never needs a probability space of its own: the limit law is bound through its distribution function, defined explicitly as the Poisson mixture `criticalBoundaryCDF beta z := sum_q poissonPMFReal r_beta q * stdNormalCDF ((z + (q - r_beta)/(3 * sqrt r_beta)) / sqrt (8/9))`, using `ProbabilityTheory.poissonPMFReal` (`Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Poisson/Basic.lean:214`, `= exp(-r) r^n / n!`) with `poissonPMFReal_nonneg`/`_pos` and `hasSum_one_poissonMeasure` (`:63`) for total mass one, plus `Causalean.Mathlib.stdNormalCDF`. This makes 'variance one, nonzero third cumulant, hence not N(0,1)' and 'F_beta is continuous' elementary computations on an explicit absolutely convergent series -- no weak-convergence-on-measures apparatus. The binomial-to-Poisson pointwise mass limit that the proof of `thm:repeated-star-boundary` needs for `H_n ~ Bin(m_n, p_n)` is REUSED verbatim: `ProbabilityTheory.tendsto_choose_mul_pow_of_tendsto_mul_atTop` (`Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/Poisson/PoissonLimitThm.lean:70`, `n.choose k * p n ^ k * (1 - p n) ^ (n - k) -> exp(-r) r^k / k!` from `n * p n -> r`), composed with the index change `n |-> m_n` (gap to bridge: `m_n -> atTop` and `m_n * p_n -> r_beta`; the deprecated measure-valued variant `binomial_tendsto_poissonPMFReal_atTop` (`:94`) should NOT be used). Search trace: `Glob .lake/packages/mathlib/Mathlib/Probability/Distributions/*.lean` initially showed no Poisson file, which would have been a FALSE absence -- re-grepped `Mathlib/Probability` for `poissonPMF|Poisson` and found the `Poisson/` subdirectory with both files.
\(G_n\) is a simple undirected graph on \(\mathcal I_n\).

nl.statement: For each connected component of \(G_n\), take a positive unit-norm Perron eigenvector of the component block of \(\mathcal H_n\), assign ranks by decreasing coordinate with label ties, and concatenate components by their smallest label. This defines the unit-to-rank map \(\pi_n\), its inverse \(\rho_n=\pi_n^{-1}\), and \(B_{n,i}=\{j:\{i,j\}\in G_n,\ \pi_n(j)<\pi_n(i)\}\).

review.note: Unfolding PerronOrderData shows positive unit-norm component Perron vectors, least-label component representatives, decreasing-coordinate ranks with label tie-breaking, and least-label component concatenation; rho is the inverse permutation and B is exactly earlierNeighbors, both determined by the returned rank.

nl.statement: Independently for \(i\in\mathcal I_n\), draw \(U_{n,i}=1\) and \(U_{n,i}=0\) with probability \((4\lambda_n)^{-1}\) each and draw \(U_{n,i}=*\) with probability \(t_n=1-(2\lambda_n)^{-1}\); set \(E_{n,i,k}=\{U_{n,i}=k,\ U_{n,j}=*\text{ for all }j\in B_{n,i}\}\) and \(q_{n,i}=(4\lambda_n)^{-1}t_n^{|B_{n,i}|}\).

review.note: Unfolding prodDesign, tritDesign, and tritMass gives independent coordinates with masses (4λ_n)⁻¹, (4λ_n)⁻¹, and 1-(2λ_n)⁻¹, while the companion exposureEvent and exposureProb definitions give exactly E_{n,i,k} and q_{n,i}.

nl.statement: Apply Algorithm 1 of \cite{KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024CGD} with \(r=2\), formal direct-effect conflict graph \(\mathcal H_n\), rank map \(\pi_n\), and coordinates \(U_{n,i}\) to obtain \(Z_n\); the strict earlier-neighbor sets are \(B_{n,i}\) from \(G_n\). On \(E_{n,i,1}\) the algorithm realizes \(\mathbf e_{n,i}\) in unit \(i\)'s closed \(G_n\)-neighborhood, and on \(E_{n,i,0}\) it realizes \(\mathbf 0_n\) there.

review.note: Unfolding cgdState and cgdStep yields the r=2 direct-effect CGD assignment: a unit is treated exactly when its coordinate is one and every earlier neighbor is star, while all other coordinates remain control, which gives both stated exposure-event realizations.

After unfolding observedOutcome, eventIndicator, exposureEvent, and exposureProb, cgdEstimator is exactly the displayed Horvitz–Thompson formula for T_n, and the companion directEffect definition is exactly the displayed τ_n.

nl.statement: \[\mathcal M_n(d;B,c)=\left\{(G_n,Y_n):\ G_n\text{ is simple and undirected},\ Y_n\text{ satisfies arbitrary neighborhood interference on }G_n,\ D_n\le d,\ \frac1n\sum_i|a_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \frac1n\sum_i|b_{n,i}|^4\le B,\ \sigma_n^2\ge\frac{c\lambda_n}{n}\right\}.\]

nl.statement:
Let \((X_s,\mathcal G_s)_{s=1}^N\) be a finite real martingale-difference sequence such that \(\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E X_s^2=1\) and \(\mathbb E|X_s|^4<\infty\).  There is a universal finite constant \(C\) such that, with \(S_N=\sum_{s=1}^N X_s\) and \(\langle S\rangle_N=\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E[X_s^2\mid\mathcal G_{s-1}]\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|\mathbb P(S_N\le x)-\Phi(x)\right|
 \le C\left\{\sum_{s=1}^N\mathbb E|X_s|^4+
 \mathbb E|\langle S\rangle_N-1|^2\right\}^{1/5}.
\]

review.note: The cited logical carrier self-containedly quantifies finite real martingale differences, normalization, fourth-moment integrability, predictable quadratic variation, one universal positive finite constant, and the p=2 exponent 1/5.

nl.statement:
For fixed \(B\ge1\), \(0<c\le1\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), let \(((G_n,Y_n))_{n\ge1}\) be any sequence such that \((G_n,Y_n)\in\mathcal M_n(D_n;B,c)\) for every \(n\).  The graph-adaptive condition
\[
 \frac{D_n^2}{n\lambda_n}\longrightarrow0
\]
is sufficient for
\[
 d_{\mathrm K}\left(\frac{T_n-\tau_n}{\sigma_n},Z_0\right)\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat{\mathrm{VB}}_n}{\mathrm{VB}_n}
 \xrightarrow{\mathbb P_U}1,
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P_U(\tau_n\in C_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha.
\]
For the repeated-star construction at any fixed \(\beta>0\), the same diagnostic converges instead to \(\beta^{3/2}>0\), while the standardized estimator converges to \(\mathcal L_{\beta}\ne\mathcal N(0,1)\).  Thus the repeated-star family is a nonvanishing-diagnostic elbow illustration; the sufficient condition is not asserted to be necessary for each individual graph sequence.

review.note: After unfolding the referenced definitions, Lean exactly encodes the model-sequence diagnostic implication, Kolmogorov convergence, variance-bound ratio convergence in probability, liminf coverage bound, and the repeated-star diagnostic/CDF limit with nonnormality; β > 0 implies the stated positive limit.
